steps.body: Teens hide everywhere: an egg tray of 10 with 2 beside it, a pack plus spares. Spot the ready ten; the count is nearly done.
steps.narration: Teens hide everywhere: an egg tray of 10 with 2 beside it, a pack plus spares. Spot the ready ten; the count is nearly done.

widget.prompt: A tray already holds ten cupcakes. Add loose cupcakes until the tray holds 16 in all.

commonCounts.feedback: 0 loose cupcakes leaves 6 still missing — ten alone is only 10, not 16.
5 loose cupcakes leaves 1 still missing; ten and 5 is 15, one short of 16.
7 loose cupcakes adds 1 too many; ten and 7 is 17, one past 16.

widget.missFeedback: The ten cupcakes are done; keep adding loose ones until the tray holds 16.
widget.successFeedback: 16 cupcakes — one full tray of ten, plus 6 more loose ones.

predict.prompt: A ten-tray of eggs and 6 loose ones. Fastest true count?

options.label: Count all sixteen one by one

predict.reveal: The tray is a ready-made ten; only the loose eggs need counting.

cml.actionGoal: Build one complete ten, then count on the ones, for knb teen apply.
invariants: Every teen number is one complete ten and some ones — the left digit records the finished ten, the right digit counts the extras — and that split is what knb teen apply rests on.
misconceptions: Reading the 1 of a teen as “one” instead of one TEN, or counting only the leftover ones and forgetting the completed ten.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more dot joined the ones, which teen would the frame show then?

widget.prompt: An egg tray holds 10, and 2 eggs sit beside it. How many eggs?

options.label: 2 — the ones beside the tray
options.feedback: The tray's ten eggs count too; the extras merely ride on top of them.

options.label: 10 — the tray's worth
options.feedback: The tray alone is ten, but the two beside it lift the total to twelve.

options.label: 20 — two full trays
options.feedback: Only one tray is full; the two loose eggs are ones, not a second ten.

options.label: 12 — a tray-ten and two more
options.feedback: Correct — the full tray is a ready-made ten, so the count reads ten and 2: twelve.

widget.prompt: Start at 10 and count on 3. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 12 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 13.
14 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 3 hops from 10 to land on 13.

widget.missFeedback: Count 3 on from 10: you land on 13.
widget.successFeedback: 10 and 3 more is 13 — the teen numeral written as a walk: ten first, then the ones.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 3 counts past ten are needed to reach 13.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count-on stops after 3 numbers, on 13.

widget.prompt: Which pair is NOT a split of 16?

options.label: 10 and 6
options.feedback: 10 + 6 = 16, so this pair is a valid split of 16 — the teen split itself.

options.label: 16 and 0
options.feedback: 16 + 0 = 16, so this pair is a valid split of 16, keeping everything in one part.

options.label: 10 and 5
options.feedback: Correct — 10 + 5 = 15, one too few, so this pair is not a split of 16.

options.label: 15 and 1
